content.text: Manual order fulfillment is a trap that most creators do not recognize until it breaks at exactly the wrong moment. It functions at five sales per month. It breaks when you are asleep and a buyer in a different timezone completes a purchase and waits eight hours for a download link that should have arrived in 30 seconds. It breaks when a webhook notification gets buried in your inbox. It breaks under volume in ways that destroy buyer trust that took months to build. The automated pipeline that COREMERCH deploys eliminates every manual step permanently. When a buyer pays in crypto, NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-explained-digital-creators|COREMERCH guide to payment]]s detects the on-chain transaction and fires a webhook to your Cloudflare Worker or [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-broken-here|Digital Product]]-commerce-automation-explained-digital-7|google]] Apps Script endpoint. The backend verifies the transaction hash on the blockchain, logs the order to Supabase or Google Sheets, generates a receipt, and sends the delivery email via Resend or Gmail — all within 30 seconds of payment confirmation.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters: Google apps

The webhook is the technical mechanism that makes automated digital delivery possible at scale. When a buyer completes a crypto payment, NOWPayments monitors the blockchain and detects the incoming transaction. When the transaction receives the configured number of confirmations — typically one confirmation on Tron, which takes under 60 seconds — NOWPayments sends an HTTP POST request to the webhook endpoint URL you configured in your NOWPayments dashboard. This is the URL of your Cloudflare Worker or Google Apps Script Web App. The endpoint receives the webhook payload, validates the signature against the secret key you configured, and begins order processing immediately.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The architecture of Google Apps Script for digital commerce automation is built around a sovereign stack, which processes orders in under 30 seconds. This stack consists of Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, Supabase for order storage, and NOWPayments for automatic crypto payment verification. Each component works together seamlessly to ensure a smooth and automated digital product delivery experience.
Who This Is Built For and Why

Manual fulfillment has specific failure modes that automated systems eliminate permanently. Time zone gaps cause hours-long delivery delays when buyers in Asia or Europe purchase while the seller is asleep in Africa. Notification fatigue causes orders to go unnoticed when webhook emails are buried in an inbox. Human error causes the wrong file to be sent or the wrong buyer to receive a link. Volume spikes overwhelm a manual process that functions at low order rates but breaks under simultaneous demand. The automated pipeline handles all of these cases identically — ten simultaneous orders from buyers in different time zones are processed as ten independent webhook events, each receiving the same automated treatment within 30 seconds.
By leveraging Google Apps Script for digital commerce automation, creators can automate their online store, bypassing the limitations of traditional payment gateways.
The Components That Make It Work Together

Cloudflare Workers is the backend engine in Stack 02 deployments. It runs serverless JavaScript at the edge — code that executes in response to HTTP requests, including the incoming NOWPayments webhook. The free tier provides 100,000 requests per day, which is sufficient for the sales volume of most individual digital product sellers. Workers has no server to manage, no runtime to configure, and no infrastructure to maintain. It scales automatically and is globally distributed — the same code runs in data centers close to wherever the request originates.
